q: Name a JavaScript framework or library.

answers.l: Jordan Walke at Facebook, open-sourced in 2013. JSX was widely mocked at launch.
Evan You, 2014, after working on AngularJS at Google.
The 2016 rewrite. Same name as AngularJS, different framework.
John Resig, 2006. Still running on a huge share of the web.
Rich Harris. A compiler, so there’s little framework runtime to ship.
Vercel’s React framework.
TJ Holowaychuk, 2010. Middleware all the way down.
Miško Hevery’s original, 2010. Two-way binding and dirty checking. End of life in 2021.
Grew out of SproutCore. Convention over configuration.
Jeremy Ashkenas, 2010. Models, views and events in a few kilobytes.
Fine-grained reactivity with signals and no virtual DOM.
React’s API in about 3 KB.
The utility belt, forked from Underscore.
Mike Bostock’s Data-Driven Documents.
WebGL 3D for everyone. Started by Ricardo Cabello (mrdoob).
Dan Abramov, 2015, built for a conference talk about hot reloading and time-travel debugging.
Hypermedia first. The successor to intercooler.js.
Islands architecture: ship HTML, hydrate only what needs it.
From the React Router team.
Vue’s answer to Next.js.
React static sites with a GraphQL data layer.
Angular-style architecture for Node servers.
Steve Sanderson, 2010. MVVM and observables.
Google’s small library for Web Components, Polymer’s successor.
Behavior in HTML attributes. Its author pitched it as Tailwind for JavaScript.
Full stack and real-time by default, 2012.
Resumability instead of hydration.
Basecamp’s "modest" framework for the HTML you already have.
Jeremy Ashkenas again. Lodash’s parent.
Its docs suggest thinking of it as Lodash for events.
The date library that declared itself done in 2020 and recommended alternatives.
Mustache templates with helpers.
"Logic-less" templates.
WebSockets with fallbacks.
From Express’s authors, rebuilt around async functions.
A fast, schema-based Node web framework.
Eran Hammer at Walmart Labs, built to survive Black Friday.
Tiny, fast, with routing and XHR built in.
2004. Modules and widgets before most of the web cared.
Sam Stephenson, 2005. Extended native prototypes, which caused trouble for years.
Its Array.prototype.flatten forced TC39 to rename flatten to flat in 2018. "SmooshGate."
Effects and drag-and-drop on top of Prototype.
The Yahoo! User Interface library. Development ended in 2014.
Enterprise widgets with a desktop-app feel.
Google’s Web Components library, succeeded by Lit.
eBay’s streaming UI framework.
React-like, built for raw speed.
Small, component-based UI library.
Rob Eisenberg’s framework after he left the Angular 2 team.
Google Web Toolkit, 2006. Write Java, ship JavaScript.
A 2012 joke site that presented plain JavaScript as a framework: 0 bytes, faster than everything.
jQuery’s API without the old-IE baggage.
Apple’s framework for MobileMe. It became Ember.
Bitovi’s MVC framework, descended from JavaScriptMVC.
Shopify’s CoffeeScript MVC framework.
Palm’s framework for webOS apps.
Built at The Guardian for interactive news graphics.
A whole framework in about 1 KB.
Your app is a pure function of streams.
A lightweight MVC framework, written in CoffeeScript.
